questions.learningObjective: Explain why real multiplier is below simple
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why the real multiplier is below the simple one; explain.

answer.exemplar: Currency drains and excess reserves leak funds from the banking system, reducing expansion. Ignoring those leaks overstates the multiplier.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why bank runs threaten solvency
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why bank runs threaten banks; explain.

answer.exemplar: Banks hold only a fraction of deposits as reserves, so a sudden withdrawal wave can exhaust liquidity and force failure. Assuming full reserves ignores the fraction lent.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Spot an error in a lending claim
questions.stem: A study group revision claims lending has no effect on reserves; what is wrong?

options.text: Reserves are unaffected by all transactions

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this bank lending and deposits item is: Where do reserves go?. That is why "Lending moves reserves between banks" is right. The option "Reserves are unaffected by all transactions" (denies reserve movement) does not satisfy the rule.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain the effect of a reserve ratio decrease
questions.stem: A study group revision asks what a lower reserve ratio does; which is right?

options.misconception: confuses "It lowers the money multiplier" with the correct "It raises the money multiplier"
names "It has no effect" where the rule requires "It raises the money multiplier"

questions.explanation: A lower reserve ratio raises the multiplier by allowing more lending. The other options misstate this.
questions.hint: Does a lower ratio allow more lending?

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why deposit creation expands money
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why deposit creation expands the money supply; explain.

answer.exemplar: Each loan creates a new deposit while only a fraction is reserved, so money grows beyond the initial injection. Assuming reserves fully back deposits ignores the fraction lent.

questions.explanation: Loans create deposits while only a fraction is reserved, so money expands. Full-reserve assumptions ignore this.

questions.learningObjective: Compute reserves after a run
questions.stem: A study group revision shows reserves 1000 and withdrawals 600; what reserves remain?
questions.explanation: Applying the bank runs and reserves rule — Subtract withdrawals from reserves — yields "400". Reversing the reasoning would recover the given quantities.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute money supply from reserves
questions.stem: A study group revision gives reserves 500 and multiplier 8; what is the money supply?
questions.explanation: The rule that settles this money multiplier item is: Multiply reserves by the multiplier. That is why "4000" is the answer.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Spot an error in a central bank claim
questions.stem: A study group revision claims central bank liabilities exceed assets; what is wrong?

options.misconception: selects "Assets are always zero" instead of "Assets equal liabilities plus capital"
selects "Capital is negative" instead of "Assets equal liabilities plus capital"

questions.explanation: The balance sheet identity requires assets to equal liabilities plus capital. The revision violates this.
questions.hint: What is the balance sheet identity?

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why excess reserves rose post-crisis
questions.stem: A study group revision asks why excess reserves rose after the crisis; explain.

answer.exemplar: Banks held more excess reserves for precautionary liquidity and due to interest on reserves. Assuming reserves are always lent ignores precautionary demand.

questions.explanation: Precautionary demand and interest on reserves raised excess reserves. Assuming full lending ignores this.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain how reserve requirements reduce run risk
questions.stem: A study group revision asks how reserve requirements reduce bank run risk; which is right?

options.misconception: selects "They eliminate all risk" instead of "They ensure some liquidity is always available"

options.text: They ensure some liquidity is always available

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this bank runs and reserves item is: What do reserves provide?. That is why "They ensure some liquidity is always available" is right. The option "They raise bank profits" (confuses reserves with profits) does not satisfy the rule.
